implement.name: Naming, scope functions, extension functions, val vs var
implement.summary: val by default; var only when reassignment is the behaviour; scope and extension functions chosen by what the call site reads, not by habit

implement.name: Null-safety, platform types, and precondition functions
implement.summary: T? on every value that can be absent; !! only with a stated local proof; platform types (Java-interop T!) treated as a borrowed contract; require for arguments, check for state, error for the unreachable branch

implement.name: Coroutines, structured concurrency, scopes, dispatchers, cancellation, Flow
implement.summary: coroutineScope { } or a scoped lifetime — never GlobalScope.launch outside the bootstrap; cancellation cooperative and never swallowed; Dispatchers injected; Flow cold by default, hot types only at the seam

implement.name: data class, sealed class / sealed interface, value class
implement.summary: data class for value-shaped records with no identity; sealed class or sealed interface for closed hierarchies; value class for type-safe wrappers around a single underlying value

implement.name: Object expressions vs companion objects vs top-level functions
implement.summary: Top-level functions when no state is shared; companion object only when state or a constant-bearing factory belongs on the class; object expressions for one-off SAMs; named object for true singletons

implement.name: Visibility modifiers
implement.summary: private by default; internal as the module boundary; public only on a surface meant to cross a published boundary — never to silence a test that crossed the wrong one

review.name: Idiomatic Kotlin refusals
review.summary: val/var, null-safety and platform types, coroutines and Flow, data/sealed/value classes, object vs companion vs top-level, and visibility — each finding citing the rule it breaks

find-spec.name: Where a Kotlin-language rule lives
find-spec.summary: A reviewer tracing a Kotlin rule to its source reads the six rules in plugins/scrumia-kotlin/rules/ and the upstream Kotlin documentation each one cites
